messages:
alex_k: Quick heads-up — dedicated capacity update: starting this week we're rolling out H100S-80GB pools in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. :tada:
maria_p: Nice! Is this public for all Dedicated customers or early access?
alex_k: Initially early access + reserved rollout. GA plan: two-week pilot in us-west-2, then staggered expansion to eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-1. Explanation below.
noah_r: Any changes to allocation policy? Customers will want to know burst behavior.
alex_k: Yes — new policy: burst pools are enabled by default for Dedicated accounts with active reserved capacity. Key points:
- New "burst" buckets let workloads exceed baseline up to 2x for short windows (max 30m).
- Burst uses spare physical capacity; not guaranteed during high cluster demand.
- We added per-org burst quotas; request increases via Console or SE.

maria_p: Timeline?
alex_k: Timeline: us-west-2 pilot available Mon 2025-03-25 (console toggle + API), eu-central-1 pilot 2025-04-08, ap-southeast-1 tentative 2025-04-22. GA for all regions expected early May.

ops-bot: deploy:capacity-pools: h100s-pool-usw2 created by infra-ci at 2025-03-24T17:12:05Z

sahil_m: How do teams reserve H100S for a customer? Any CLI/console steps?
alex_k: Two ways:
1) Console: Admin -> Dedicated -> Capacity -> Reserve -> select GPU type: "H100S-80GB" -> region -> quantity -> review -> confirm.
2) CLI example:
```
redwood dedicated reserve --org my-org --region us-west-2 --gpu H100S-80GB --count 8 --term 1m
```
Note: reservations are soft-checked immediately; final provisioning can take up to 2 hours in pilot zones.

maria_p: Any perf/cost notes?
alex_k: Performance: expect ~25-40% lower p99 decode latency for long context generative workloads vs A100-40GB on our tests; cost: unit price higher, but improved throughput means better cost/token in many LLM serving patterns. Full perf profiles & quantization knobs: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated/h100s-perf (internal)

noah_r: Is there an automated migration path for customers pinned to older model variants?
alex_k: We'll provide an in-console migration assistant that suggests compatible model/quantization pairs and a canary rollout plan (A/B percent split + auto-fallback to baseline). SEs will get a preview next week.

maria_p: What about AZ coverage? Any single-AZ risks?
alex_k: For now pools are per-availability-zone: us-west-2a/b and eu-central-1a/b depending on data center capacity. Customers wanting cross-AZ redundancy should reserve in two AZs and enable automatic failover in the Dedicated settings.

ops-bot: note: capacity-notice email triggered for orgs with reservations expiring in <7d

sahil_m: Are we changing default quotas?
alex_k: Default GPU quota per org stays same for now. We added a new quota for "burst slots" (opt-out possible). To increase quotas, open a support ticket or go through your AM.

maria_p: Who owns the rollout communication to customers? I can draft the email and console banner.
alex_k: Can you take it? Target GA announcement + migration guide. cc @sales and @solutions.

maria_p: On it. Draft will include sample billing impact, migration steps, and how to request early access.

noah_r: Anything for SRE/infra on-call?
alex_k: Yes — infra will get a playbook for capacity shortages and preemptive scaling. SRE action items live in the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-capacity-h100s (internal).

maria_p: One more — are we enabling telemetry flags for customers by default?
alex_k: Telemetry collection for H100S pools is opt-out. We added a checkbox on reserve flow and a tenant-level flag.

maria_p: Great. thanks everyone.

noah_r: :thumbsup:
